long_biography.plain_text:
Nidal Ghazi Karameh, known professionally as Mofid Karameh, trained as a mechanical engineer before moving to Nigeria. He established Mikano International in the early 1990s, initially importing, servicing and maintaining generators. The business changed course when it began assembling generating sets locally, turning technical service experience into an industrial platform rooted in Nigerian manufacturing.

Karameh later broadened Mikano beyond power equipment. Steel fabrication and electrical systems were joined by heavy machinery, vehicle assembly, construction, food production and medical manufacturing. He continued to lead the group as chairman and chief executive, while the move into locally produced diagnostic equipment extended the same manufacturing approach into healthcare.

uncertainties: Companies House uses the legal name Nidal Ghazi Karameh, while Mikano and business reporting use Mofid Karameh. An indexed European International Council listing explicitly uses Nidal Mofid Karameh and identifies him as Mikano's chairman, while registry-derived Nigerian company data links Nidal Ghazi Karameh to Mikano. The naming convention is not authoritatively explained, so identity confidence remains high rather than very high.

The European International Council page was indexed with the identity bridge but was not directly retrievable at review time, so it is retained only as a tier-three orientation source and is corroborated by the legal, corporate and business-source matches.
No dedicated Forbes profile was found for Nidal Ghazi, Nidal Chazi, Nidal Mofid or Mofid Karameh. The 2022 Forbes Africa interview is a direct feature, not a profile.

Mikano's operating portfolio is clearly multi-sector, but consolidated ownership, financial accounts and segment values are not public. Diversified reflects documented operating breadth rather than a quantified personal net-worth allocation.

Companies House shows that Omar Nidal Karameh owns at least 75 per cent of the UK affiliate while Nidal retains director-appointment rights. That affiliate structure was not extrapolated to the Nigerian parent or wider group.

The precise birthplace was not established at the required confidence and is not proposed. The source record's Syrian birth country and Syrian secondary nationality were preserved but not used to infer a city.

The 20 June birth day is supported by Mikano's official same-day 60th-birthday announcement and independently corroborated by Companies House's June 1965 record; it remains a proposed field pending human review.

The existing Instagram and Twitter links use the Mofid name but were not independently re-proposed. No verified personal Facebook, YouTube, TikTok or dedicated personal website was found. Only the LinkedIn profile directly tagged by Mikano and linked by FactCheckHub was proposed.
Blank suffix and secondary-residence fields were treated as optional, while death, internal-notes and unknown-name fields were treated as inapplicable while alive or system-controlled.
